subject: Dedicated capacity: Zenith rush request and allocation prioritization
messages:
From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@zenith.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity request: Q1 committed pool

Hi Rishi,

Following up from our call — Zenith is planning a Q1 launch for our in-product assistant and we need a reserved pool for inference. High-level ask:
- 40 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved starting Jan 01 (flexible on exact instance types)
- Target sustained concurrency: 250 rps; peak bursts ~500 rps for short windows
- Latency SLO: 99th < 350ms for streaming responses
- Minimum 12-month commitment preferred; need pricing and prelim SLOs by next week to review with procurement

I attached our capacity request and a usage estimate. Can we get a rough feasibility answer and a ballpark of cost and lead time by 12/3? We can move fast on contract if numbers align.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Novak
Head of Platform | Zenith AI
elena.novak@zenith.ai
Attachment: zenith_capacity_request.pdf; zenith_usage_estimate.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@zenith.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: Q1 committed pool

Elena — thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick acknowledgements and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size properly:
- Is the 40-GPU request a steady pool (always reserved) or a 40-GPU ceil that you expect to average lower across the month?
- Do you expect multi-model routing (different model families) or a single model serving profile?
- Is prepayment an option for you (we can materially shorten lead time with upfront commit)?

We have two active large renewals that overlap with your window (OrionCloud renewal and an internal reserved pool for an existing enterprise customer). I want to be transparent that we have tight Q1 capacity; I will loop in Infrastructure and Product Ops to map out options and tradeoffs. Can we do a 30-min call Monday to review options?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Zenith capacity request — urgent allocation decision needed

Following up — Zenith (Prospect) sent the attached ask for 40 A100-eq GPUs starting Jan 1, with a 12-month preferred commit. They say they can move fast on contract if we can show feasibility + pricing by 12/3.

Context: we have an existing renewal conversation with OrionCloud scheduled for late Dec; they currently have a reserved pool that we expected to reclaim and reallocate at the beginning of Q1. If we shift that pool to a new commit (Zenith), OrionCloud's rollout will be delayed ~4–6 weeks unless we provide temporary burst capacity.

As this is a clear cross-customer contention scenario, need your recommendations on:
1) What fraction of the 40 GPUs we can realistically commit by Jan 1 without violating current SLAs?
2) Lead time and operational risk for a temporary burst/overflow (e.g., allow Zenith to burst onto shared fleet for first 6 weeks)
3) Commercial levers we should require (prepayment, minimum spend, phased ramp)

Please reply with options and numbers — this is time-sensitive.

—Rishi
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zenith capacity request — urgent allocation decision needed

Quick capacity note and three options (numbers are approximate; I'll validate with infra tomorrow):
Current state (Q1 baseline):
- Committed dedicated pools: 210 A100-eq GPUs (across 6 enterprise tenants)
- Unallocated reserved capacity scheduled for Jan 1 reclamation: ~48 A100-eq GPUs (this is the OrionCloud tranche we discussed)
- Shared/overprovisionable fleet headroom (burstable): ~20 A100-eq GPUs (depends on batch/latency mix)

Options:
A) Full commit to Zenith for 40 GPUs on Jan 1:
   - Impact: OrionCloud gets delayed or must accept degraded throughput until we free capacity (~4–6 weeks).
   - Operational risk: Medium-high; needs prepayment + contracted ramp to justify.
B) Split commit (preferred operational compromise):
   - Reserve 20 GPUs dedicated to Zenith on Jan 1 (guaranteed) + allow up to 20 GPUs burst on shared fleet for up to 6 weeks.
   - Impact: OrionCloud experiences a smaller delay (2–3 weeks for full roll), and we avoid breaking existing SLAs.
   - Requirements: 6–8 week burst SLA (best-effort), signed 12-month contract, 50% of Q1 invoice up front.
C) Phased delivery contingent on incremental capacity build:
   - Hold initial firm commit to 8–10 GPUs Jan 1, ramp to 40 over 60 days as more capacity comes online or other customers renew.
   - Impact: Lowest risk operationally; requires Zenith to accept staged go-live.

If Sales wants to keep Orion fully on schedule, we can offer Zenith a time-limited burst (option B) with tightened commercial terms (higher per-GPU per-month for burst). Need leadership sign-off on credits to Orion if we nudge their schedule.

I can run a tighter cost/latency simulation tomorrow and attach an SLO-split proposal.

—Karthik
VP, Infra & Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zenith capacity request — urgent allocation decision needed

I reviewed Karthik's options — I recommend we prioritize current customers (OrionCloud) for scheduled rollouts unless we get outsized commercial protection from the new deal. Proposal:
- Offer Zenith option B (20 guaranteed + 20 burst) with a commercial package: 12-month term, 50% Q1 prepay, and a higher unit rate on burst capacity (20% premium).
- Commit to a one-time service credit (equivalent of 2 weeks of committed capacity) to OrionCloud if their full rollout is delayed because of this reallocation. That keeps the renewal motion intact.
- Require Zenith to accept a phased SLA: guaranteed pool for initial launch, full pool delivered by day 45 after contract execution.

Rationale: preserves renewals, gives sales a path to close Zenith quickly, and reduces infra operational risk. Rishi — please present these commercial terms to Elena and procurement. If Zenith pushes back on prepay, we can escalate to business ops for a modified payment plan but will need to reduce guaranteed pool.

CC: Dylan for ops readiness and for finalizing burst guardrails.

—Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@zenith.ai>, procurement <procurement@zenith.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: Q1 committed pool — preliminary path forward

Elena / team — thanks for the fast response. Internal alignment complete and we have a preliminary operational + commercial path we can take to meet your Jan 1 launch while protecting our existing customers. High level: 

1) Temporary operational split (Option B):
   - 20 A100-equivalent GPUs guaranteed reserved for Zenith starting Jan 1.
   - Up to 20 A100-equivalent GPUs allowed as a burst onto shared fleet for up to six weeks from Jan 1, subject to burst guardrails and per-minute throttles to protect latency SLOs for existing customers.
2) Commercial terms required to enable burst and prioritize allocation:
   - 12-month commitment (standard Redwood MSA + SOW)
   - 50% of Q1 spend prepayment upfront at contract signature
   - Burst capacity billed at 20% premium to protected reserved rate
3) Delivery milestones:
   - Guaranteed 20 GPUs live Jan 1
   - Remaining capacity phased to full 40 by day 45 after signature

I attached a short SLO split that Karthik prepared (proposed_slo_split.pdf). Please review and let me know if procurement can confirm the prepay and term by 12/03 — if so, we'll move to contract and schedule a go/no-go for Jan 1. If the prepay is a blocker, we can discuss a smaller guaranteed pool on the same timeline.

Thanks — will keep you posted on any changes. CC'ing our infra/product leads to finalize operational guardrails.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Attachment: proposed_slo_split.pdf
